title: Adaptive prompt-slice generator and low-latency runner shim for stable profile publishing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: When generating performance profiles for new model variants (especially quantized/low-latency builds), our benchmark harness produces noisy profile artifacts due to wide prompt variant combinatorics and nondeterministic sampling across runners. This makes stable pinning and catalog publishing brittle.

Goal: Implement an adaptive prompt-slice generator that deterministically selects a small, representative set of prompt variants per workload slice, combined with a lightweight runner shim that enforces seedbanked deterministic execution and standardized telemetry for low-latency model builds. Deliverables: (1) prompt-slice generator library with fingerprinting and seedbank support, (2) runner shim that normalizes timing and cache priming across local and cloud runners, (3) updated profile publisher that embeds slice provenance and seed metadata to enable reproducible profile rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Prompt-slice generator produces <= 200 prompt variants per profile with explainable selection rationale (coverage score >= 0.85)
Runner shim guarantees deterministic response ordering and seeded randomness for eval runners (replayable with same seedbank) across at least 3 model backends: fp32, int8, and optimized-kernel build
Published performance profiles include prompt-slice fingerprint, seedbank id, runner-shim version, and validation run hash
Automated end-to-end smoke runs reproduce published throughput/latency within +/- 7% on test infra
Integration tests exercising the harness fail only for intentional regression thresholds and produce actionable diff reports
tasks: Design prompt-slice selection algorithm (coverage heuristics + rarity downsampling)
Implement fingerprinting schema and seedbank integration
Build runner shim for deterministic timers, priming, and KV-cache warmup hooks
Add telemetry schema changes to profile publisher and catalog metadata
Write unit and e2e tests for reproducibility and diffable artifacts
Run cross-backend validation matrix and collect baseline artifacts
Document library usage and onboarding steps for model teams
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chosen hybrid sampling approach (coverage-first then rarity-based downsample) to balance representativeness and variant count
2026-03-04: Decided runner shim will be user-space lightweight wrapper (no kernel changes) to remain deployable in Hosted/Dedicated/Private
2026-03-07: Opted to publish seedbank ids in profile metadata rather than raw seeds for security and compactness
risks: Deterministic runner shim may mask real-world nondeterminism if applied too aggressively (risk: false sense of reproducibility)
Reducing variant count could miss rare failure modes for some workload slices
Integration complexity across many eval runners (third-party/backported runners) could delay adoption
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint collisions and slice stability (target < 1 collision per 100k slices)
E2E reproducibility runs on ci-hw-1 against fp32/int8/opt-kernel builds
A/B comparison job that compares published profile to baseline profile and emits token-level diffs
Chaos job: run with runner-shim disabled to surface masked nondeterminism before publishing
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (internal): enable prompt-slice generator + runner shim in harness-internal only, publish to staging catalog
Stage 2 (canary): select 3 active model onboarding flows to auto-generate profiles using new pipeline and collect telemetry for 5 days
Stage 3 (opt-in): allow model teams to opt-in via config flag; gather feedback
Stage 4 (global): flip default to new generator + shim and require seedbank id in profile metadata for all published profiles
notes: Implementation must be careful to avoid leaking PII in prompt fingerprints — fingerprints should be hash-only with prefix metadata
Telemetry should separate priming latency from steady-state token latency to avoid skewing tail metrics
We should align seedbank format with existing eval-runner seed conventions (see ENG-512304)
